draft.shortGloss: to finish; to end; to run out
draft.emotion: relieved and satisfied to finally have something done
notes: Takes '-isc-' in most present-tense forms: 'finisco, finisci, finisce, finiamo, finite, finiscono'.
In compound tenses, it takes 'avere' when transitive ('ho finito il libro', I finished the book) and 'essere' when intransitive ('il film è finito', the movie has ended).
Followed by 'di' before an infinitive: 'ho finito di mangiare' (I finished eating).

examples.translation: I decided to finish the book tonight.
examples.emotion: determined and focused on reaching the goal

senses.definition: To come to an end, or to have nothing left of a supply.

examples.text: È finito il latte, dobbiamo comprarlo.
examples.translation: The milk has run out, we need to buy some.
